!86 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Four panes, one source. Every pane compiles it; none rejects the resources\0A// declared inside the constant buffers.\0A//\0A// What to compare is the \22Buffer Definitions\22 comment block that FXC and the two\0A// DXC panes print, and specifically the Offset column of the scalar field that\0A// follows each buffer member, plus the Size reported for each constant buffer.\0A//\0A// FXC (ps_5_0) places that scalar field at offset 0 in all four constant buffers\0A// and reports each of them as 4 bytes.\0A//\0A// Both DXC panes place it at offset 12 in the second constant buffer and at offset\0A// 64 in the third, and report those two buffers as 16 and 68 bytes: a\0A// StructuredBuffer member consumes the size of its element type in the constant\0A// buffer. The fourth buffer, whose member is a typed Buffer rather than a\0A// StructuredBuffer, is laid out the way FXC lays it out.\0A//\0A// So the same source produces two different host-side constant-buffer layouts, and\0A// neither compiler says anything about it.\0A//\0A// The clang-dxc pane runs the front end only. Its diagnostics are all about the\0A// implicit uint-to-float4 conversions in the return statement, which is what shows\0A// that Sema did resolve the members of all four buffers; it says nothing about the\0A// resources inside them.\0A//\0A// Note the Resource Bindings table: the buffers are never read in this shader, so\0A// neither compiler emits a t# binding for them. The 1.6 pane's remark about a\0A// missing DXIL.dll is Compiler Explorer's environment, not this shader.\0A//\0A// Local evidence -- 20 stable DXC releases, the DXIL validator's verdict on the\0A// container, and the reflection the runtime would see -- is in the issue's triage\0A// directory.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// The entry point and target profile are needed to compile this example:\0A// -T ps_6_6 -E PSMain -Fh test.h test.hlsl\0Astruct ModelData // Size: 4 Bytes\0A{\0A    uint myInt; // Offset: 0 Bytes\0A};\0Astruct ModelData2 // Size: 16 Bytes\0A{\0A    StructuredBuffer<float3> bufferData;\0A    uint myInt; // Offset: 12 Bytes\0A};\0Astruct ModelData3 // Size: 68 Bytes\0A{\0A    StructuredBuffer<float4x4> bufferData;\0A    uint myInt; // Offset: 64 Bytes\0A};\0Astruct ModelData4 // Size: 4 Bytes\0A{\0A    Buffer<float4> bufferData;\0A    uint myInt; // Offset: 0 Bytes\0A};\0Acbuffer __cbModelData  { ModelData  cbModelData;  };\0Acbuffer __cbModelData2 { ModelData2 cbModelData2; };\0Acbuffer __cbModelData3 { ModelData3 cbModelData3; };\0Acbuffer __cbModelData4 { ModelData4 cbModelData4; };\0Astruct PSInput\0A{\0A    float4 position : SV_Position;\0A    float4 color    : COLOR0;\0A};\0Afloat4 PSMain(PSInput input) : SV_Target0\0A{\0A    return input.color * cbModelData.myInt * cbModelData2.myInt * cbModelData3.myInt * cbModelData4.myInt;\0A}\0A"}

!86 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Four panes, one source. Every pane compiles it; none rejects the resources\0A// declared inside the constant buffers.\0A//\0A// What to compare is the \22Buffer Definitions\22 comment block that FXC and the two\0A// DXC panes print, and specifically the Offset column of the scalar field that\0A// follows each buffer member, plus the Size reported for each constant buffer.\0A//\0A// FXC (ps_5_0) places that scalar field at offset 0 in all four constant buffers\0A// and reports each of them as 4 bytes.\0A//\0A// Both DXC panes place it at offset 12 in the second constant buffer and at offset\0A// 64 in the third, and report those two buffers as 16 and 68 bytes: a\0A// StructuredBuffer member consumes the size of its element type in the constant\0A// buffer. The fourth buffer, whose member is a typed Buffer rather than a\0A// StructuredBuffer, is laid out the way FXC lays it out.\0A//\0A// So the same source produces two different host-side constant-buffer layouts, and\0A// neither compiler says anything about it.\0A//\0A// The clang-dxc pane runs the front end only. Its diagnostics are all about the\0A// implicit uint-to-float4 conversions in the return statement, which is what shows\0A// that Sema did resolve the members of all four buffers; it says nothing about the\0A// resources inside them.\0A//\0A// Note the Resource Bindings table: the buffers are never read in this shader, so\0A// neither compiler emits a t# binding for them. The 1.6 pane's remark about a\0A// missing DXIL.dll is Compiler Explorer's environment, not this shader.\0A//\0A// Local evidence -- 20 stable DXC releases, the DXIL validator's verdict on the\0A// container, and the reflection the runtime would see -- is in the issue's triage\0A// directory.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// The entry point and target profile are needed to compile this example:\0A// -T ps_6_6 -E PSMain -Fh test.h test.hlsl\0Astruct ModelData // Size: 4 Bytes\0A{\0A    uint myInt; // Offset: 0 Bytes\0A};\0Astruct ModelData2 // Size: 16 Bytes\0A{\0A    StructuredBuffer<float3> bufferData;\0A    uint myInt; // Offset: 12 Bytes\0A};\0Astruct ModelData3 // Size: 68 Bytes\0A{\0A    StructuredBuffer<float4x4> bufferData;\0A    uint myInt; // Offset: 64 Bytes\0A};\0Astruct ModelData4 // Size: 4 Bytes\0A{\0A    Buffer<float4> bufferData;\0A    uint myInt; // Offset: 0 Bytes\0A};\0Acbuffer __cbModelData  { ModelData  cbModelData;  };\0Acbuffer __cbModelData2 { ModelData2 cbModelData2; };\0Acbuffer __cbModelData3 { ModelData3 cbModelData3; };\0Acbuffer __cbModelData4 { ModelData4 cbModelData4; };\0Astruct PSInput\0A{\0A    float4 position : SV_Position;\0A    float4 color    : COLOR0;\0A};\0Afloat4 PSMain(PSInput input) : SV_Target0\0A{\0A    return input.color * cbModelData.myInt * cbModelData2.myInt * cbModelData3.myInt * cbModelData4.myInt;\0A}\0A"}
